title: Why Smart People Make Bad Money Decisions
desc: Nobel prize winners, brilliant professionals and legendary investors have all made surprisingly bad money decisions. Get comfortable and join me for a calm, 2.5-hour journey into why: the fund that was too clever to fail, the bat and the ball, why confident people trade too much, the less we know, following the crowd, what we lived through, Concorde and sunk costs, black 26 times in a row, too many choices, checking too often, the experts, the planes that came back, emotions and money, famous mistakes, the illusion of understanding, the price of a house, the IKEA effect, staying put, the company you know, the optimism of founders, the fear of regret, the premortem, base rates, a calm decision checklist and the quiet creep. We end with a slow wind-down, so you can fall asleep to the last part if you like. Educational only, not financial advice.
